chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises: should he pray when he wakes up, or should he wait until the sun has spread? He said: "He prays when he wakes up." I said: Should he perform the witr or pray the two rak'ahs? He said: "No, rather he begins with the obligatory prayer."

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer, here referring to a supererogatory prayer
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer time, referring here to salat al-fajr
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer that must be performed first
key_terms.تَبْزُغَ: to rise, referring to the sun's appearance

ai.seo_question: If someone sleeps through salat al-ghadah until sunrise, should he pray immediately upon waking or wait?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who misses the morning salat due to sleep until after sunrise. It instructs that he should perform the obligatory prayer immediately upon waking and not begin with supererogatory prayers before making up the missed obligation.
